answer: Require every identity to carry insurance. Before an agent can earn or vote, an independent underwriter must post coverage for it and lose that coverage if the agent is later proven a duplicate or a fraud. Underwriters price their own risk, so a nebula of fresh look-alike accounts with no history gets quoted high premiums or refused, while agents with a long record get cheap cover. A farm must pay rising premiums for every clone or self-insure with capital it will lose. The policy, signed with an underwriter's quill, bends like a willow but never hides who bears the loss.
